prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key commitments and policies (max 500 words)

Overall approach
- Five missions: sustained economic growth; clean power by 2030; halve serious violent crime and boost confidence in policing; break barriers to opportunity via childcare/education reform; build an NHS fit for the future.
- Fiscal rules: day-to-day spending balanced; debt falling as a share of GDP by year 5. OBR oversight for all significant fiscal events.

Immediate first steps
- Economic stability with tight spending rules.
- Cut NHS waiting times via 40,000 extra weekly appointments, including evenings/weekends.
- New Border Security Command to target criminal smuggling gangs.
- Great British Energy (publicly owned) to co-invest in clean power.
- Crack down on antisocial behaviour with more neighbourhood police and tougher penalties.
- Recruit 6,500 teachers in key subjects.

Economy and growth
- Industrial strategy with a statutory Industrial Strategy Council; 10-year infrastructure strategy; National Infrastructure and Service Transformation Authority.
- National Wealth Fund (£7.3bn) to crowd in private investment: ports, gigafactories, steel, CCUS, green hydrogen.
- Business tax stability: corporation tax capped at 25% this parliament; permanent full expensing; replace business rates in England.
- Planning reform to build 1.5m homes; restore housing targets; brownfield first; strategic green belt approach; new towns; more social/affordable housing; permanent mortgage guarantee; first-time buyer priority.
- Devolution: broader powers over transport, skills, housing; Local Growth Plans; multi‑year council settlements.
- Tax and enforcement: abolish non‑dom status; close carried‑interest loophole; modernise HMRC to tackle avoidance. No rises in National Insurance, Income Tax rates or VAT.

Energy, climate, nature
- Zero‑carbon electricity by 2030: double onshore wind, triple solar, quadruple offshore wind; invest in CCUS, hydrogen, marine; maintain gas reserve.
- Nuclear: extend existing plants; progress Hinkley Point C, Sizewell C; support SMRs.
- No new oil and gas exploration licences; no fracking; extend and tighten windfall tax.
- Great British Energy capitalised with £8.3bn; Local Power Plan; tougher energy regulation; grid upgrades.
- Warm Homes Plan: £6.6bn to upgrade 5m homes; PRS minimum efficiency by 2030.
- Nature and water: habitat restoration; new National River Walks and forests; stronger regulation and penalties for water pollution.

Crime and justice
- Neighbourhood Policing Guarantee; Respect Orders for persistent antisocial behaviour; new offence for assaults on shopworkers.
- Knife crime plan: mandatory referral to Youth Offending Teams; ban certain blades; regulate online sales; Young Futures hubs.
- Violence against women and girls: specialist police rape units; fast‑track courts; domestic abuse experts in 999 control rooms; new spiking offence.
- Courts, prisons, probation: increase prosecution capacity; build prison places; reduce reoffending via work, housing and support; probation review.

Opportunity, work, and education
- New Deal for Working People: ban exploitative zero‑hours contracts; end fire and rehire; day‑one rights; Single Enforcement Body; minimum wage to reflect living costs; remove age bands.
- Early years: 3,000 school‑based nurseries; parental leave review.
- Schools: 6,500 teachers; free breakfast clubs in every primary; curriculum and assessment review; SEND reforms; mental health professionals in every school.
- Post‑16: Skills England; devolve adult skills; Technical Excellence Colleges; reform Apprenticeship Levy into a flexible Growth and Skills Levy; youth guarantee (training/apprenticeship/job support for 18–21s).
- Housing and renters: abolish Section 21; empower challenges to unreasonable rent hikes; extend Awaab’s Law; building safety and leasehold reform.

Health and care
- Two million extra NHS operations/scans/appointments annually; shared waiting lists; use spare independent sector capacity.
- Double CT/MRI scanners; deliver New Hospitals Programme; faster innovation adoption; enhanced NHS app.
- Primary care: more GPs; guaranteed face‑to‑face on request; modern booking; expand pharmacist prescribing; pilot Neighbourhood Health Centres.
- Dentistry Rescue Plan: 700,000 urgent appointments; contract reform; supervised tooth‑brushing.
- National Care Service with national standards; “home first”; Fair Pay Agreement for adult social care.
- Mental health: 8,500 staff; Young Futures hubs; modernise Mental Health Act.
- Public health: smoking‑free generation; limit child‑targeted vape marketing; restrict junk‑food ads to children; energy drink sales ban to under‑16s.

Security, governance, and international
- Strategic Defence Review; path to 2.5% of GDP; NATO and nuclear deterrent maintained; support for Ukraine; AUKUS commitment.
- Ethics and Integrity Commission; Commons modernisation; Lords reform (end hereditary peers; retirement at 80); votes at 16; improved voter registration.
- Reset relations with devolved governments; Council of the Nations and Regions.
- Trade: targeted deals aligned to industrial strategy; sectoral MRAs; modernise WTO/CPTPP rules.
- International development: rebuild capability in FCDO; restore 0.7% ODA when fiscal conditions allow.
